To enhance cheque security and reduce the risk of unauthorised transactions, we would ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- To view this message in HTML format, click here: https://t6.connect.au.bank.in/r/?id=t6a335948,44c8ef5,ff3ea6&p1=%40E%2FmLRpcGD%2BUMYt5UKMWOGsuJU6W16IdkURq2I01PojQ%3D or paste this link in a Web browser ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- Dear Customer, Greetings from AU Small Finance Bank. To enhance cheque security and reduce the risk of unauthorised transactions, we would like to inform you of an important update regarding cheque payments. In line with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) guidelines on the Positive Pay System for cheques, issued vide RBI circular no. RBI/2020-21/41 DPSS.CO.RPPD.No.309/04.07.005/2020-21 dated September 25, 2020, banks are advised to implement Positive Pay for high-value cheques to enhance customer safety and reduce cheque-related fraud. Therefore, with effect from 1st July 2026, Positive Pay confirmation will be mandatory for all cheque issuances of ₹10 Lakh and more. What is Positive Pay? Positive Pay is a security feature where the cheque issuer confirms key cheque details (such as cheque number, date, amount, and beneficiary name) with the Bank before the cheque is presented for clearing. Important to Note - Positive Pay confirmation is mandatory for cheques of ₹10 Lakh and more - Any cheque of value ₹10 Lakh and more presented without Positive Pay confirmation will be returned unpaid - This measure is being implemented to prevent cheque frauds and unauthorized alterations How to Submit Positive Pay Confirmation Positive Pay details can be submitted through: - Net Banking or AU 0101 App - https://t6.connect.au.bank.in/r/?id=t6a335948,44c8ef5,ff3ea7 Click here to submit now. - AU Website - https://t6.connect.au.bank.in/r/?id=t6a335948,44c8ef5,ff3ea8 Click here to submit now. For any assistance or clarification, please visit your nearest branch or contact us at 1800 1200 1200 . Looking forward to always offering you the best of our services. records.snippet: If you are unable to view this message correctly, click here Dear Customer, Greetings from AU Small Finance Bank. To enhance cheque security and reduce the risk of unauthorised transactions, we would
records.rawEvidence: Mandatory Positive Pay Confirmation for High‑Value Cheques – Effective 1 Jul 2026 If you are unable to view this message correctly, click here Dear Customer, Greetings from AU Small Finance Bank. To enhance cheque security and reduce the risk of unauthorised transactions, we would ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- To view this message in HTML format, click here: https://t6.connect.au.bank.in/r/?id=t5e8001ca,445f71b,f7df1c&p1=%40bK1ZL9zVL%2Bs4PQvtWA2VyEeWsrBp%2Bmh1SWH%2BMxylkFo%3D or paste this link in a Web browser ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- Dear Customer, Greetings from AU Small Finance Bank. To enhance cheque security and reduce the risk of unauthorised transactions, we would like to inform you of an important update regarding cheque payments. In line with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) guidelines on the Positive Pay System for cheques, issued vide RBI circular no. RBI/2020-21/41 DPSS.CO.RPPD.No.309/04.07.005/2020-21 dated September 25, 2020, banks are advised to implement Positive Pay for high-value cheques to enhance customer safety and reduce cheque-related fraud. Therefore, with effect from 1st July 2026, Positive Pay confirmation will be mandatory for all cheque issuances of ₹10 Lakh and more. What is Positive Pay? Positive Pay is a security feature where the cheque issuer confirms key cheque details (such as cheque number, date, amount, and beneficiary name) with the Bank before the cheque is presented for clearing. Important to Note - Positive Pay confirmation is mandatory for cheques of ₹10 Lakh and more - Any cheque of value ₹10 Lakh and more presented without Positive Pay confirmation will be returned unpaid - This measure is being implemented to prevent cheque frauds and unauthorized alterations How to Submit Positive Pay Confirmation Positive Pay details can be submitted through: - Net Banking or AU 0101 App - https://t6.connect.au.bank.in/r/?id=t5e8001ca,445f71b,f7df1d Click here to submit now. - AU Website - https://t6.connect.au.bank.in/r/?id=t5e8001ca,445f71b,f7df1e Click here to submit now. For any assistance or clarification, please visit your nearest branch or contact us at 1800 1200 1200 . Looking forward to always offering you the best of our services. To protect your accounts from fraud, follow these simple password protection habits: Create a strong password: Use letters + numbers + special characters. Avoid your name/nickname, date of birth, and simple patterns (like 1234). Use two-factor authentication wherever available. Keep passwords separate: Use Unique passwords for banking, email, and social media accounts. Never share: your personal and banking details (even with bank staff). Change your password regularly, or if you notice anything unusual. Avoid saving passwords on public/shared devices or web browsers. records.rawEvidence: Sankranti & Groundhog Day: what’s the connection? 🌞 How we mark the return of the sun. ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ It’s still sweater season. Mornings are still a tug-of-war between the blanket and our better instincts. But look closer, Shailesh. The days are longer, the sunlight is warmer. The coconut oil in the kitchen is beginning to wobble. As we wait for winter to retreat and spring to awaken, let’s talk about festivals that celebrate the return of the sun between January and March. Around The World in Five Festivals #1 India’s Sankranti (and its many cousins) What it is: Pan-Indian harvest festival marking the sun’s northward journey (Uttarayana) and the end of winter. Celebrated regionally as different festivals: Sankranti, Pongal, Lohri, Magh Bihu, Tusu Parab, Uttarayana. How it’s marked: Bonfires, kite-flying, rangoli/kolam decorations, worship of the sun and cattle. Festive foods: Chakkara pongal, til-gud laddoos, chikkis, sugarcane, seasonal pithas, khichdi, ellu-bella. Sankranti Staples: Interestingly, across all these varied regional festivals, recipes keep circling around the same seasonal ingredients. » Freshly harvested rice and millets » Jaggery (in blocks, powder, or liquid) » Fresh-pressed ghee » Til (sesame) and groundnuts » Sugarcane, bananas, and seasonal fruits » Lentils and pulses #2 Iran’s Sadeh What it is: An ancient fire festival symbolising the triumph of warmth and light over cold. In Persian, ‘sadeh’ means ‘hundred’ and it is believed that 100 days remain for the arrival of spring. How it’s marked: Community bonfires, farmers preparing fields for planting, prayers for the strengthening sun. Festive foods: Nuts, dried fruits, sweet breads, winter stews. #3 Scotland’s Up Helly Aa What it is: A Viking-inspired winter festival celebrating the end of long nights and the return of daylight. How it’s marked: Torchlight parades, Viking squads, and the burning of a ceremonial longship. Festive foods: Hearty stews, roast meats, oatcakes, winter puddings. #4 Ireland’s Imbolc What it is: A festival of early spring, honouring the first signs of renewal after winter. How it’s marked: Candle lighting, visiting holy wells, early spring cleaning traditions. records.rawEvidence: 🚫 .apk files = instant access to your phone 🛡️Safe Banking starts with informed choices️ If you are unable to view this message correctly, click here Dear Customer, Fraudsters share fake links on SMS, WhatsApp, or email, posing as bank alerts, e 🛡️Safe Banking starts with informed choices️ ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- To view this message in HTML format, click here: https://t13.mailers.hdfcbank.net/r/?id=tf2bc6a06-e9d3-4457-a226-97c4df1bb424,1b9964,7c2d7&e=cDE9JTQwZDhaNDRFWXolMkJ5c3BNdHNWV0NOYkVnNXZnNUhhQjFpWW5nZkVObmNmWDU0V3I3ZjglMkZMSmRVd0ljTFolMkJxNkVtQjk1SHI0N2hCMGJ5ZWp2b1YwY1VPMkElM0QlM0Q&s=hCSi3be6x6yh81jPjgiQg59VK2zpvgaKgjalb5MPRsQ or paste this link in a Web browser ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- Dear Customer, Fraudsters share fake links on SMS, WhatsApp, or email, posing as bank alerts, e-challans, or official notices. The link asks you to download an APK file ( through an app outside the Play Store) , which ,once clicked and installed , can then access your personal and banking details, control your phone, and drain your bank account. Stay protected from fake APK files by following these 5 habits: Download Only from Trusted Sources: Always install banking apps from official stores like the Google Play Store or Apple App Store. Avoid Suspicious Links & Attachments: Never click on unverified links or download attachments from unknown sources. Check App Permissions: Be cautious of apps that request SMS, call log, or contact access. Enable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA): Use secure login methods like OTPs, biometrics, or authentication apps. Report Fraud Attempts: Suspected Fake Call, SMS, or WhatsApp? Report at https://t13.mailers.hdfcbank.net/r/?id=tf2bc6a06-e9d3-4457-a226-97c4df1bb424,1b9964,7c2de https://t13.mailers.hdfcbank.net/r/?id=tf2bc6a06-e9d3-4457-a226-97c4df1bb424,1b9964,7c2df (Chakshu portal) or via the Sanchar Saathi app. If You're a Victim: Act fast - contact your bank, visit https://t13.mailers.hdfcbank.net/r/?id=tf2bc6a06-e9d3-4457-a226-97c4df1bb424,1b9964,7c2e0 https://t13.mailers.hdfcbank.net/r/?id=tf2bc6a06-e9d3-4457-a226-97c4df1bb424,1b9964,7c2e1 or call 1930 . https://t13.mailers.hdfcbank.net/r/?id=tf2bc6a06-e9d3-4457-a226-97c4df1bb424,1b9964,7c2e2 Watch Now >> *Terms and conditions apply https://t13.mailers.hdfcbank.net/r/?id=tf2bc6a06-e9d3-4457-a226-97c4df1bb424,1b9964,7c2e3&e=cDE9JTQwVWRLVkVqOGx4UXV0d0JndzVNTGhMNWkwRndQQWs2NWQ

Cranberry Supports urinary tract health and is antioxidant-rich. ORDER SOME Closer home, desi berries Amla Ayurveda’s darling, amla deserves all the hype it gets! Ber (Indian jujube) You may have noticed these red-coloured berries adorning roadsides in the winter. This sweet, chewy fruit is high in fibre, and great for digestion and steady energy. records.subject: Stay Alert: Protect Yourself from Social Engineering Scams
records.snippet: Dear Customer, Fraudsters are using increasingly sophisticated techniques to trick customers into sharing sensitive information. One such method is social engineering, where scammers impersonate
records.rawEvidence: Stay Alert: Protect Yourself from Social Engineering Scams Dear Customer, Fraudsters are using increasingly sophisticated techniques to trick customers into sharing sensitive information. One such method is social engineering, where scammers impersonate IDFC FIRST Bank Dear Customer, Fraudsters are using increasingly sophisticated techniques to trick customers into sharing sensitive information. One such method is social engineering, where scammers impersonate trusted entities like banks/ card issuers etc. to gain your confidence. How these scams work: Fraudsters may call you claiming some suspicious transactions in your account. They often use personal details like your name, email, postcode, or partial card number to appear genuine. You may also receive authentic-looking SMS or notifications while on the call with them, making the scam seem legitimate. They may pressure you to share full debit/credit card details, OTPs, or approve transactions under the pretext of “testing,” “KYC update,” “refund processing,” or “account verification.” Some fraudsters may even spoof official phone numbers or display fake caller IDs to appear credible. Increasingly, scammers use links to fake websites or apps that mimic official platforms to capture your login credentials. Important Safety Tips: Never share your confidential account/ card details, PIN, passwords, or OTPs with anyone over phone, SMS, or email, even if the caller claims to be from your Bank. Do not initiate/ confirm any transaction as genuine unless you are carrying it out yourself. Avoid downloading apps from unknown sources or links shared by callers. Banks never ask you to install third-party apps for verification. Do not click on unverified links received via SMS, email, or messaging apps. If you receive a suspicious call, hang up immediately and contact your bank using the official number. Remember: Fraudsters may use real-looking SMS or notifications to trick you. Always verify directly with your bank before taking any action. Stay vigilant and protect your money. Need help? Report any unauthorized transactions through internet/mobile banking app or contact the Bank at 1800 10 888. Please note that you can report cyber frauds related complaints to National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal https://click.emailers.idfcfirstbank.com/?qs=b7ed2ae256e4cc3585d29210488d8da4e433346a6c3dc6dda027a0ea8972438b59547bbc9e91b2f119f47c34960b16a97303404bc7e741b1cac3013b080f689f (https://cybercrime.gov.in) or call their help

records.snippet: ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Big Basket Dear Shailesh, We enjoy the fruits of their labour but rarely get to meet the farmers who grow our food. This Kisan Diwas (Dec 23), we thought you'd
records.rawEvidence: Meet Arasappa: he grows your food 🌱🌾 ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Big Basket Dear Shailesh, We enjoy the fruits of their labour but rarely get to meet the farmers who grow our food. This Kisan Diwas (Dec 23), we thought you'd ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Dear Shailesh, We enjoy the fruits of their labour but rarely get to meet the farmers who grow our food. This Kisan Diwas (Dec 23), we thought you’d like to get to know a few of our 10,000+ farmer partners. At 80+, he is our oldest farmer—but in energy and zeal, he can give youngsters tough competition! He lives in a joint family of 25 members. Grows: Carrot, beans, cauliflower, mango, coconut Comfort food: Bassaru (a leafies sambar) Fave song: The National anthem Fave movie: Bangarada Manushya (a Rajkumar superhit!) Meet Manoj. At just 24, he’s our youngest farmer! He lives with his mother and brother. Grows: Big brinjal, bottle gourd, yelakki bananas Comfort food: Ragi mudde & naati chicken curry Fave song: Bombe heluthaithe from the Puneet movie Rajakumara. Fave movie: KGF Part 2 Supranura and Girish supply a great deal of organic vegetables to us. Both are family men who live with their wives and kids. Supranura thinks gongura chutney makes everything better while Girish is a fan of veg biryani! Grows: Organic tomato, bhindi, green brinjal, turmeric, chillies, sugarcane Girish’s fave movie: Mr and Mrs Ramachari Women are an integral part of every farm’s functioning and in many cases, the lead farmers. Meet Swati, one of our women farmers. She lives with her husband and in-laws. Grows: Coriander, cabbage, bitter gourd, cauliflower Comfort food: Kofta curries Fave song: Kitna pyara tujhe rab ne banaya. Fave movie: Housefull Dhanaji farms in a high-rainfall region, which can be quite tricky. His family includes his father, wife, daughter, and son. Grows: Organic cabbage & tomato Comfort food: Puran poli Fave song: Rani phadakti lakho zende. Fave movie: Taleem (a Marathi movie about an underdog wrestler) Sukumar farms in a thickly wooded, hilly area of Wada, where he lives with his father, wife, and two sons. Grows: Bottle gourd, Cowpeas, forest bitter gourd, brinjal Comfort food: Chicken curry Fave song: Saare jahan se accha Fave movie: Border Kailash farms in a semi-arid region that sees extreme temperatures. His family includes his mother, wife, and three children. Grows: Cabbage, spring onion, local tomato Comfort food: Dal bati churma Fave song: Mere desh ki dharti Fave movie: Purab Pa

Clear blue skies, a nip in the air, and some warm winter sun on your skin—basically, picnic Emailer It’s Time for a Picnic! There’s something extra welcoming about a sunny day in the middle of winter. Clear blue skies, a nip in the air, and some warm winter sun on your skin—basically, picnic weather! It’s the season for slowing down, sharing laughs, and soaking up unhurried moments with loved ones on a cosy picnic mat. This week, we’re bringing you simple, crowd-pleasing recipes designed to make every sunlit gathering a sweet little celebration. # 1 Good Food That Travels We’ve planned this picnic like pros. Say goodbye to soggy letdowns and hello to easy-peasy dishes that travel well and taste amazing under the sun. Inside, you'll find recipes for cold sesame noodles (a vibrant, make-ahead favourite), crunchy chickpea salad, and more. # 2 Picnic-Worthy Sweet Treats Forget messy spills and dive straight into grab-and-go treats like apple cinnamon pockets, scotcharoos, and lemon bars. Perfect for sunny afternoons, they’re made to share (or maybe not!). Warning: These desserts are so good, the ants will be lining up—so make sure you pack them tight! # 3 Time for an outdoor feast! In many parts of ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Dear Shailesh, December is a time for endings and new beginnings; and if we’re lucky, relaxed work schedules and perhaps a holiday. In many parts of the world, December is also the season of giving, a time to spread sweetness and light. That’s what we want to talk about today. The bigbasket Foundation India is home to thousands of NGOs doing incredible work. Here’s what we do for them through the bigbasket Foundation. Identify and verify NGOs doing stellar work Give them a voice through our platform Donate generously to their cause Use our network to fundraise and support them Shailesh, you can support 20+ vetted NGOs that work on three causes close to our heart: KNOW MORE Spotlight: Feet of Glory In collaboration with the Tata Ultra Marathon, we joined the Feet of Glory campaign. Runners who participated dipped their feet in color to pledge a pair of shoes for underprivileged children. For every footprint made, we donated a pair of shoes and ration kits to a child in need. Children at Gerizim Rehabilitation Trust, Bengaluru opening their shoe boxes. Would you like to help? YOU Donate through the bb app NGO Receives 100% of your contribution BENEFICIARIES Get the support they urgently need YOU Enjoy tax benefits under Section 80G DONATE NOW (Shailesh, your contribution (however big or small) matters more than you think. All donations are tax-exempted as per Section 80G. The NGO will send you the receipt directly. This winter, we invite you to bask in the warm glow of giving. There’s nothing quite like it! Many thanks, The BB Foundation team P.S: Do forward this email to friends and family who might also be interested in giving. records.rawEvidence: PM’s Message for You: Every Action of Ours Should Strengthen the Constitution Dear fellow citizens, Namaste! 26th November is a day of immense pride for every Indian. It was on this very day in 1949 that the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India, a sacred Letter from the Prime Minister on Samvidhan Diwas Dear fellow citizens, Namaste! 26th November is a day of immense pride for every Indian. It was on this very day in 1949 that the Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India, a sacred document that has continued to guide the nation’s progress with clarity and conviction. That is why, nearly a decade ago, in 2015, the NDA government decided to mark 26th November as Constitution Day. It is the power of our Constitution that enabled a person like me, coming from a humble and economically disadvantaged family, to serve as the Head of the Government continuously for over 24 years. I still remember the moments in 2014, when I came to Parliament for the first time and bowed, touching the steps of the greatest temple of democracy. Again, in 2019, after the election results, when I entered the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, I bowed and placed the Constitution on my forehead as a mark of reverence. This Constitution has given several others, like me, the power to dream and the strength to work towards it. On Constitution Day, we remember all the inspiring members of the Constituent Assembly, which was presided over by Dr. Rajendra Prasad, who contributed to the making of the Constitution. We recall the efforts of Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar, who chaired the Drafting Committee with remarkable foresight. Several distinguished women members of the Constituent Assembly enriched the Constitution with their thoughtful interventions and visionary perspectives. My mind goes back to the year 2010. This was when the Constitution of India completed 60 years. Sadly, the occasion did not receive the attention it deserved at a national level. But, to express our collective gratitude and commitment to the Constitution, we organised a ‘Samvidhan Gaurav Yatra’ in Gujarat. Our Constitution was placed on an elephant and I, along with several other people from different walks of life, had the honour of being part of the procession. When the Constitution completed 75 years, we decided that this would be an extraordinary milestone for the people of India. But today, we have a range of appliances to heat, clean, boil, fry, and what-have-you! Basically, to keep us perfectly comfy in our homes all winter long. In this edition, we’re looking at home appliances that make all the difference when temperatures dip. #1: Electric Kettle Able to boil water faster than a gas stove, a kettle is a trusty ally that saves you cooking time any time of the year. Come winter, it’s a true hero. Whether you’re whipping up hot cocoa, brewing a herbal tea, or prepping cup noodles, it speeds up things—and makes you wonder how you ever got by without it! ELECTRIC KETTLES #2: Air Fryer Much like the monsoons, winter brings with it sudden snack cravings. Which means, Shailesh, it’s air fryer season! Air fryers work just like convection ovens, by circulating superheated air containing tiny droplets of oil. This mimics the effect of deep frying but with significantly fewer calories. What can you make with it? For the Indian kitchen: samosas, roasted peanuts/makhanas, pani puri, French fries, cakes, popcorn, papads, even your regular sabzis—all with zero-to-minimal oil usage. AIR FRYERS #3: Vacuum Cleaner Winter might feel cleaner (crisp air and all), but it isn’t really. Indoors, it’s quite the opposite. Closed windows, dry air, and static electricity mean dust settles faster and sticks harder. Throw in pet fur and dust allergies into the mix—and you might need more than a mop and broom to keep the house clean. records.rawEvidence: Spooky season stories 👻 Inside: Desi ghosts stories ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ “This really happened to my cousin!” Shailesh, if you’re like most of us, you’ve heard at least one ghost story that started this way. Swapping ghost stories at sleepovers was an essential part of most of our childhoods. But in case you missed this rite of passage, we’re here to fill you in. Today, in the spirit of Halloween, we’re recollecting India’s best spooky tales. Brace yourself, Shailesh. The Naale Baa witch - Karnataka Before Bengaluru was home to India’s IT folks, it was home to the ‘90s era ‘Naale Baa’ witch, who supposedly roamed the streets at night knocking on doors. But if you scrawled “Naale Baa” (‘come tomorrow’) on your door, she’d respect your schedule and move on. Source Aleya lights - Sundarbans Strange ghostly lights seen over the marshes of Sundarbans, supposed to be the spirits of fishermen who died. (Science says that it’s an optical illusion caused by gases, but we’ll ignore this boring fact today.) Woman in white - Delhi cantonment A woman clad in a white sari hails motorists for a lift. If you don’t stop, she chases your car, running as fast as your vehicle. But it is said, if you stop, she just vanishes—which just goes to show the importance of good manners. The ghost of Major Charles Burton - Brijraj Bhavan, Kota Rajasthan’s most polite ghost is a British officer who reportedly haunts the heritage hotel of Brijraj Bhavan. It is said that he never disturbs guests, but can be quite the poltergeist with guards who slumber while on duty. This list would be incomplete with a mention of the ubiquitous banyan tree ghost of every small town in India. The rules for engaging with these ghosts are usually the same—don’t whistle, don’t look back, and don’t visit after dark! The Halloween Origin Story - Keep the ghosts guessing! Shailesh, if you’ve ever wondered how a festival celebrating ghosts came to be, here’s the story. Halloween was originally an ancient Celtic festival that marked the start of winter. People believed that, in this transition, the boundary between the living and the dead grew thin. So people lit bonfires and wore disguises to confuse these spirits. We understand the importance of feeling safe while banking. Fraudsters are finding new ways to trick customers, but a little awareness can help you stop them and keep your banking experience safe & worry-free. Frauds You Should Know About And How to Stay Protected: Type of Fraud What Happens How to Stay Safe 1. APK Fraud Fraudsters send fake app links via SMS or WhatsApp. Once installed, they can access your phone and misuse your personal data. Do: Download apps only from the Play Store or App Store. Don’t: Click on unknown links or files sent by unknown sources. 2. Investment Fraud Fraudsters promise very high profits through fake trading or investment websites. Do: Invest only through SEBI-registered platforms. Don’t: Believe offers that sound “too good to be true.” 3. Digital Arrest Fraud Fraudsters impersonate police or government officials and threaten false legal action to collect money. There is no such thing as a “digital arrest” under Indian law. Do: Stay calm and hang up immediately. Don’t: Share personal details or transfer money to unknown callers. 4. Job Offer Fraud Fraudsters offer fake job opportunities and ask for fees or banking details. Do: Verify the company’s authenticity before applying. Don’t: Pay for job offers or share your Bank Account details. 5. Parcel Delivery Fraud Fraudsters claim your parcel contains illegal items and demand payment to avoid fake legal action. Do: Contact the courier company directly using official contact details. Don’t: Panic or make any payment without confirming with the courier company. https://t13.mailers.hdfcbank.net/r/?id=t5455ebc5-9cf5-4971-abc4-f9dcc10adb2e,10dc2c,4078e&e=dXRtX21lZGl1bT1FbWFpbCZjb

records.rawEvidence: Think Before You Click — One Tap Can Let Malware In Dear Customer, From a friendly-looking app to a surprise message with an attachment — malware often hides where you least expect it. Once inside your device, it can: • Steal your personal data, OTPs, IDFC FIRST Bank Dear Customer, From a friendly-looking app to a surprise message with an attachment — malware often hides where you least expect it. Once inside your device, it can: -Steal your personal data, OTPs, and banking information -Spy on your activities and capture passwords -Lock your device using ransomware -Drain your account or misuse your identity Your digital world deserves the same protection as your home.. Safe Digital Practices to Follow: Download apps only from official app stores. Avoid third-party sites or unknown sources. Don’t open links or attachments from unverified senders. Keep your operating system, browsers, and apps updated to close security loopholes. Use trusted antivirus software and schedule regular scans. Avoid connecting to public Wi-Fi networks. Enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) wherever possible. Never install APKs from unverified sources like WhatsApp, Telegram, or similar platforms. Every click counts — make sure yours is a safe one. Together, let’s build a malware-free digital world. Need help? Report any unauthorized transactions through internet/mobile banking app or contact the Bank at 1800 10 888. Please note that you can report cyber frauds related complaints to National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal https://click.emailers.idfcfirstbank.com/?qs=881e84b54767bc957994e3d4a073b46e68cb40484d551cf3300ab1f734a307ab2eb29c74001171d1a9792b35d3fef3fc40c52dc294674ab3ea8c92a7498cbdd4 (https://cybercrime.gov.in) or call their helpline number 1930. records.snippet: Dear Customer, As the festive season approaches, we're delighted to see you embrace the celebrations with joy and cheer. But with surge in online activity during this time, fraudsters are stepping
records.rawEvidence: 🚨 Stay Safe This Festive Season: Protect Yourself from Money Mule Scams! 🚨 Dear Customer, As the festive season approaches, we're delighted to see you embrace the celebrations with joy and cheer. But with surge in online activity during this time, fraudsters are stepping IDFC FIRST Bank Dear Customer, As the festive season approaches, we’re delighted to see you embrace the celebrations with joy and cheer. But with surge in online activity during this time, fraudsters are stepping up their efforts to deceive individuals through Money Mule Scams. What is a Money Mule Scam? A money mule scam involves criminals using unsuspecting individuals to transfer stolen or illegal funds. Scammers lure victims with promises of easy money and convince them to move money through their bank accounts. By participating, you could unknowingly become a money mule, aiding criminals in illegal activities like fraud or money laundering. Getting involved in such scams, even unknowingly could lead to serious legal and financial consequences. How do fraudsters operate? Fraudsters contact customers via emails, chat rooms, job websites or blogs, and convince them to receive money into their bank accounts, in exchange of attractive commissions. The fraudsters then transfer the illegal money into the money mule’s account. The money mule is then directed to transfer the money to another money mule’s account – starting a chain that ultimately results in the money getting transferred to the fraudster’s account. When such frauds are reported, the money mule becomes the target of police investigations. How to Protect Yourself: Ignore suspicious emails or messages: Do not respond to emails, messages, or posts asking you to share your bank details or receive money on someone else’s behalf. Be cautious of unsolicited job offers: Verify the identity and contact details of any employer, especially for overseas jobs or work-from-home opportunities that involve handling money. Think twice about 'easy money' offers: If someone offers you an attractive offer/ commission to receive or transfer funds, it is likely a scam. Do not let anyone misuse your bank account. Say No to Third-Party Transactions: Never allow anyone to use your account to send or receive money, even if they claim it’s urgent. Never disclose personal/ confidential details: Do not share personal or financial information to unknown parties, especially if they ask for bank account details or copies of identification documents. records.subject: Shailesh vs. Cobwebs - the war is on!
records.rawEvidence: Shailesh vs. Cobwebs - the war is on! Pre-festival cleaning, decor, and more. ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Shailesh, Diwali doesn’t start with a bang. It starts with a dust cloth and a vacuum cleaner weeks in advance—basically, right about now! Across cultures and countries, many festivals have a pre-cleaning ritual associated with them. The reasons are often religious or symbolic. It is believed that cleaning makes your home ready to receive good energy and blessings. More ready to receive sudden guests too, we might add! For many of us, the prospect of sprucing up the house at one go is overwhelming. Shailesh, let’s cut it down to size! Today, we’re going about it in stages: first we declutter, then we clean, and then, we doll up our home for Diwali! Step 1: Conquer Clutter Clutter is a fact of life there’s no getting away from. It’s sneaky, and it’s everywhere: look away for a couple of days, and it will simply take over your house. Apart from the aesthetics, clutter can really affect your physical and mental well-being. Source Here’s how to change that this Diwali: 1. Start small, finish fast. Set a 15-minute timer and sort out a shelf, a room corner, or that pile of somethings on the table. This is way more effective and morale-boosting than trying to declutter your entire house at one go. 2. You don’t need it ‘just in case’. Donate or recycle chipped crockery, clothes you haven’t worn for over a year, books in your never-will-read pile...you get the drift. To paraphrase a popular saying: If you don’t love something, just let it go already. 3. Organize as you go Use baskets, boxes, or organizers to keep surfaces tidy. In other words, put a pretty face on the clutter you do want to keep. ORGANIZERS Bonus tip: Get help Do you struggle with letting stuff go? Try a professional decluttering service. They know their job and won’t get stuck gazing at old photo albums and letters! Step 2: Dust Begone! Shailesh, if you’re forever waging war against dust (which Indian home isn’t!), these ideas may come in handy. Cleaning Quick wins » Pick the surfaces guests notice first (for example, the coffee table or the shoe cabinet) and give them a wipe-down. » Cleaning fan blades? Slip an old pillowcase over each blade and pull—dust comes off inside the case, and there’s no mess. » A spritz of vinegar +

From late-night cravings to homestyle experiments, they’ve forever been the ultimate comfort fix. So, we’re dedicating this edition to all things noodly, saucy, and oh-so-satisfying. Time to level up your noodle game! # 1 Hunger ka Instant Fix 2025’s instant noodle scene is buzzing. Think smoky Japanese yakisoba, gochujang ramen, and Korean volcano carbonara—all ready in 3 minutes flat! Today, we’ve rounded up our top-rated favourites just for you. So, grab a fork and dig in. # 2 Homemade Asian Comfort Remember those at-home noodle experiments with soy sauce, vinegar, and a dash of masala? This time, we’re turning up the flavour with Asian recipes that deliver the real deal—from Cantonese-style chow mein to Vietnam’s tangy shrimp noodles, enjoy homemade comfort without the restaurant tab. # 3 Think you can wok the talk? Then share your favourite recipes for a chance to win a bb gift card worth Rs. 500 Contest ends on: 16 September 2025 # 4 Noodle Recipe Inspirations Powered By Spread the word! Love, All of us at bigbasket Click here to opt-out Did you ever imagine that the freshest of fruits and vegetables, top quality pulses and food grains, dairy products and hundreds of branded items could be handpicked and delivered to your home, all at the click of a button? India’s first comprehensive online megastore, bigbasket.com, brings a whopping 20000+ products with more than 1000 brands, to over 4 million happy customers. From household cleaning products to beauty and makeup, bigbasket has everything you need for your daily needs. bigbasket.com is convenience personified We’ve taken away all the stress associated with shopping for daily essentials, and you can now order all your household products and even buy groceries online without travelling long distances or standing in serpentine queues. Add to this the convenience of finding all your requirements at one single source, along with great savings, and you will realize that bigbasket- India’s largest online supermarket, has revolutionized the way India shops for groceries. Online grocery shopping has never been easier. Need things fresh? Whether it’s fruits and vegetables or dairy and meat, we have this covered as well!

records.rawEvidence: Your grandma was right. ☔ How to stay healthy during the rains ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Movies have convinced us that there’s magic in the rains. That anything is possible (romance, poetry, road trips) if you’re fueled by chai and the pitter-patter of rain. Until...reality hits. Itchy throat, sniffly nose, and bam! You’re nursing a miserable cold. It’s not just bad luck, Shailesh. We do tend to get sick more often during the monsoons because warmth, high humidity, and temperature fluctuations are the ideal setup for pathogens to grow. So today, let’s talk about how you can stay healthy this rainy season. Monsoon Menus Rainy season recommendations from around the world Source What to eat How it helps Ayurveda Warm, spiced, cooked foods (such as khichdi, pongal with cumin, pepper etc) Shop khichdi mixes Cooked food supports weak digestion and prevents toxin buildup (ama in ayurvedic terms). Spices boost immunity. Ayurveda & Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) Steamed vegetables Shop veggies Easy to digest, reduces dampness and heaviness. Ayurveda & TCM Herbal teas (ginger-tulsi, cinnamon, licorice etc) Shop herbal teas Improves circulation, boosts immunity. Mediterranean Soups & broths, legume-based dishes (minestrone, lentil broth, chickpea stew etc) Shop soups Provides warmth, hydration, protein and other essential nutrients. “But I am craving hot, crispy bajjis! ” It’s not you, Shailesh—it’s science. As outside temperature dips, your body’s core temperature decreases slightly too. You begin to crave calorie-dense foods that can provide quick energy. Ergo, the call of pakodas, bajji, vada, and more! SHOP MONSOON SNACKS Pro Tip: Drink More Water In rainy weather, our thirst signals get a bit fuzzy. You may not feel thirsty but your body’s losing fluids as usual. So carry a bottle, set reminders, do what it takes to drink enough water. records.rawEvidence: Tales of Rakhi 🧵 Recipe Contest & More 🪔 The Rakhi Edition There's nobody quite like a sibling. No one else understands you inside out the way they do—even if they fought you for the TV remote, bathroom primetime, the bigger slice of cake The Rakhi Edition There’s nobody quite like a sibling. No one else understands you inside out the way they do—even if they fought you for the TV remote, bathroom primetime, the bigger slice of cake, and just about everything else! This Raksha Bandhan, join us as we celebrate sibling bonds with festive recipes and heartwarming tales. # 1 Tales Woven in Thread Did you know that Rabindranath Tagore used the humble Rakhi as a power move—to oppose the Bengal partition of 1905? Across history and mythology, Rakhi’s simple thread has woven timeless legends. Dive into the past with us to explore these fascinating stories. # 2 Memories with Mithaas We think the best Raksha Bandhan gifts are the ones you can eat! This year, swap store-bought sweet boxes for ghee-infused delicacies made at home. Try our recipes for melt-in-the-mouth nankhatai, irresistible ghee cakes, and more. The sweet memories will linger long after the festivities end! # 3 What’s cooking in your kitchen this Raksha Bandhan? Share your recipes for a chance to win a bb gift card worth Rs. 500 Contest ends on: 12 August 2025 # 4 Rakhi Recipe Inspirations Powered By Spread the word! Love, All of us at bigbasket Click here to opt-out Did you ever imagine that the freshest of fruits and vegetables, top quality pulses and food grains, dairy products and hundreds of branded items could be handpicked and delivered to your home, all at the click of a button? India’s first comprehensive online megastore, bigbasket.com, brings a whopping 20000+ products with more than 1000 brands, to over 4 million happy customers. From household cleaning products to beauty and makeup, bigbasket has everything you need for your daily needs. bigbasket.com is convenience personified We’ve taken away all the stress associated with shopping for daily essentials, and you can now order all your household products and even buy groceries online without travelling long distances or standing in serpentine queues. Add to this the convenience of finding all your requirements at one single source, along with great savings, and you will realize that bigbasket- India’s largest online supermarket, has revolutionized the way India shops for groceries. records.subject: Beware of Fake e-challan Scam
records.snippet: Dear Customer, We want to alert you about a rising number of fake e-challan scams targeting citizens, where scammers send fake e-challan payment messages via SMS or WhatsApp, to trick users into paying
records.rawEvidence: Beware of Fake e-challan Scam Dear Customer, We want to alert you about a rising number of fake e-challan scams targeting citizens, where scammers send fake e-challan payment messages via SMS or WhatsApp, to trick users into paying IDFC FIRST Bank Dear Customer, We want to alert you about a rising number of fake e-challan scams targeting citizens, where scammers send fake e-challan payment messages via SMS or WhatsApp, to trick users into paying fines or stealing personal information. These messages contain malicious links that direct users to fake websites that look similar to official e-challan portal/ website or even prompt the users to download .APK files containing malware that can compromise your bank account/s and other personal information when you click on the link/file. How the scam works: Fake SMS/WhatsApp messages: Scamsters impersonating official traffic authorities send text messages demanding payment for traffic violations. Phishing links: The message usually has a link that the customer is asked to click and make the payment online. The link takes the customer to a fake website where they are prompted to provide their personal and financial information. Malicious APK files: Some scams involve sending a malicious .APK file (Android Package Kit) that, when installed, gives scammers access to your device, including your contacts, SMS messages, and banking apps. Sense of urgency: These messages often create a sense of urgency to pressure victims into immediate action. Scamsters also try to scare customers with threatening calls and messages from numbers that appear as ‘Traffic Control Room’, ‘E-Challan Recover’, etc. on phone apps. Tips to stay safe against fake e-challan scams: Check the sender's number or email address. Official e-challans come from recognized government sources. Look for the “.gov.in” domain in any link claiming to be from a government source. These links often do not end with “.gov.in”, which is a key sign of authenticity. Verify your traffic challan dues and make payments through the official website of traffic police department i.e., https://click.emailers.idfcfirstbank.com/?qs=c3132b1d430eb3645da9fc96b9aa7d062535bf5ba9e14ea6daaefbeea0e100e2a1fcf61b58ad824f9b8ecdd053a942681aa3ba58bae08bc4c429f56aae277c2f https://click.emailers.idfcfirstbank.com/?qs=c3132b1d430eb3645da9fc96b9aa7d062535bf5ba9e14ea6daaefbeea0e100e2a1fcf61b58ad824f9b8ecdd053a942681aa3ba58bae08bc4c429f56aae277c2f . records.rawEvidence: Shailesh, can noodles be good for you? 🍜 ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Big Basket Noodles have a bit of a reputation: super convenient, super delicious, but not quite what the doctor ordered. Made of refined flour and deep-fried before ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Noodles have a bit of a reputation: super convenient, super delicious, but not quite what the doctor ordered. Made of refined flour and deep-fried before packaging, instant noodles often serve up an undesirable nutritional profile—low fibre, empty calories, and high saturated fats. But luckily for us, not always. Enter: Oodles of healthy noodles! There’s a new wave of noodles taking over—and these are reimagining the basics to make this dish healthier. Redeem your noodles in 4 easy steps Switch the guilt out for veggies and protein. Not ready to give up on good ol’ 2-minute noodles? You can still ‘healthify’ it and lift it out of junk food territory. 1. Add veggies Add bell peppers, babycorn, broccoli, carrots, or whatever source of fibre you can find in your fridge. SHOP VEGGIES 2. Add a protein Tofu, paneer, eggs, chicken—almost anything will work, when sauteed and added as a topping to your noodles. SHOP PROTEINS 3. Go easy on ketchup It’s no secret that ketchups are usually loaded with salt, sugar, and mysterious additives. Swap it for a nutty satay sauce or chilli oil. SHOP HEALTHY DIPS AND SAUCES 4. Tone down the seasoning Seasonings are often very high in salt. If you need to control your sodium intake, use only part of the flavour pack, and substitute it with your own fresh/dried herbs and spices. Because you can never have too many noodle recipes... Here are some created by bigbasketeers, from the canteen-staple Egg Noodles, to the lip-smacking American Chopsuey, experimental noodle cones and even noodle cheelas. CHECK OUT OUR NOODLE RECIPES And you Shailesh, how do you like your noodles? If you have a specific way of dishing up noodles that you swear by, tell us! TELL US Shailesh, are you noodle-folk too? records.subject: You helped us go green in 2024, Shailesh! ♻️🤗
records.snippet: ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Big Basket Dear Shailesh, Every year, usually around World Environment Day (June 5), we bring you a round-up of the steady efforts we're taking towards a greener
records.rawEvidence: You helped us go green in 2024, Shailesh! ♻️🤗 ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Big Basket Dear Shailesh, Every year, usually around World Environment Day (June 5), we bring you a round-up of the steady efforts we're taking towards a greener ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ Dear Shailesh, Every year, usually around World Environment Day (June 5), we bring you a round-up of the steady efforts we’re taking towards a greener, more inclusive tomorrow. Six Key Areas of Impact We’re sharing details on each of these below. If you have ideas or suggestions for what else we could do, please write to me: ceo@bigbasket.com Moving Forward, Sustainably Shailesh, roughly one in every three vehicles in our delivery fleet is now electric. That’s 7431 EVs delivering your groceries, up by 12% from last year. This shift has helped us prevent nearly 15,000 tonnes of carbon emissions in 2024—the equivalent of planting and raising 2.4 lakh trees for ten years! Powered by the Sun Solar panels installed on the roof of bigbasket warehouses. We’ve installed solar panels in 25 warehouses all over India. Together, they generate 466 MWh of power every month, which is used towards meeting the warehouses’ energy requirements. This has helped us avoid 3289 tonnes of carbon emissions last year—the equivalent of planting and raising 54,384 trees for ten years. This impact remains roughly the same as last year. Supporting Organic Farming Shailesh, we continue to work closely with organic farmers, not just as suppliers, but as partners in a longer journey. Today, 7000+ organic farmers are part of our network, with 2200+ actively supplying fresh, chemical-free produce last year. » Rural livelihoods: We’ve identified and trained local youth to work as jaivikmitras (organic farming guides). They are employed at 12 collection centres dedicated to organic produce. » Agri-intelligence: Our team of agronomists continue to support farmers align crop cycles to forecasted demand and helping them through the process of organic certification. Reducing, Reusing, Recycling Starting June 2025, we’re piloting a new circular process for the paper bags and cardboard boxes that carry your orders. You will now be gently prompted to return delivery bags during handover—bags that are then inspected and either reused at the store or sent for recycling. Behind the scenes, each step will be tracked, right down to city-wise dashboards and local recycling partnerships. Building a truly inclusive workforce Shaile

records.snippet: An Epic Food Tour From Morocco to Indonesia, Ethiopia to Iran—there's a portal to the world that runs through your kitchen. This week, we're taking your palate on a global tour. Come, explore
records.rawEvidence: Global Kitchen 🌍 Recipe Contest & More ✈️ An Epic Food Tour From Morocco to Indonesia, Ethiopia to Iran—there's a portal to the world that runs through your kitchen. This week, we're taking your palate on a global tour. Come, explore Emailer An Epic Food Tour From Morocco to Indonesia, Ethiopia to Iran—there’s a portal to the world that runs through your kitchen. This week, we’re taking your palate on a global tour. Come, explore with us a world of flavour and culinary traditions from far-off cultures. # 1 The Foodie Bucket List First stop on our journey through exotic tastes: the rich, aromatic spices of Ethiopia with Misir Wat, a hearty lentil dish. Then, we'll whisk you away to Morocco for the tender, complex flavours of Chicken Tagine. And that's just the beginning—we’ve got many more stops along the way. Let’s go! # 2 Around the World in 4 Desserts Whether you fancy a sweet Spanish Churro or a crisp Australian Pavlova with a marshmallowy heart, you needn’t travel halfway across the world to taste it. Our recipes will take your sweet tooth on an adventure. records.rawEvidence: Travel Advisory Dear IndiGo Customer, This is an IMPORTANT message with reference to your upcoming domestic flight. As per latest guidelines issued by the State of Maharashtra, it is mandatory for all customers Dear IndiGo Customer, This is an IMPORTANT message with reference to your upcoming domestic flight. As per latest guidelines issued by the State of Maharashtra, it is mandatory for all customers travelling to Maharashtra to carry RT-PCR negative reports not older than 72 hours or a Covid vaccination final certificate, issued after 2 doses of vaccination and have completed 15 days after receiving the 2nd dose. Customers travelling without a valid RT-PCR negative test report or vaccination final certificate, shall be denied boarding at the departure airport. If you are travelling on a connecting flight and transiting Maharashtra, then please refer to the guidelines of your final destination arrival state. For passengers transiting from any international sectors, guidelines for the first port of entry in India will also be applicable. For exemptions and more details on State regulations, please click https://bit.ly/3dC9zT5 . To book a test through our partner, Stemz healthcare, click https://bit.ly/35zqHnZ . Looking forward to welcoming you on board our lean, clean flying machine. Regards, IndiGo
